validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/OWNERSHIP/DUPLICATE all confirmed. The pipeline is item 1 under 'PARTIALLY COMMISSIONED COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE' in PNGRB's current monthly line-wise register (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, edition 31 May 2026; large multi-column PDF, url_verifier 200s and false-negatives on every keyword per the documented large-PDF pattern in scripts/url_verifier.py -- confirmed manually via `curl -I` live 200 + `pdftotext -layout`, verbatim row read: 'Mehsana - Bhatinda   GIGL   07.07.2011   1,943   83.1   83.1   4.7   6   1,339   604   0   0   0   Jun-26   GJ,RJ,HR & PB'). This is the regulator's own authorised-pipeline register, which by definition only lists real, PNGRB-authorised common-carrier transmission assets -- confirms EXISTENCE, PipelineType=transmission, Fuel=Gas (the register is exclusively natural-gas transmission pipelines), and StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=India, StartState/Province=Gujarat, EndState/Province=Punjab (register lists states passed through as 'GJ,RJ,HR & PB', matching Mehsana/Gujarat start and Bhatinda/Punjab end). OWNERSHIP cross-checked against a source independent of both GEM and the wiki's own cited BSE-hosted GSPL annual report: CARE Ratings' credit-rating press release on GSPL India Gasnet Limited (GIGL), dated 30 August 2024 (https://www.careratings.com/upload/CompanyFiles/PR/202408130847_GSPL_India_Gasnet_Limited.pdf; same large-PDF url_verifier false-negative, confirmed manually via `pdftotext -layout`), states verbatim: 'GIGL's majority stake holder, GSPL, has 52% stake... IOCL, having 26% stake in GIGL... BPCL, having 11% stake in GIGL... HPCL, having 11% stake in GIGL' -- an exact match to GEM's Owner1-4 split (Gujarat State Petronet 52%, Indian Oil Corp 26%, BPCL Group 11%, Hindustan Petroleum 11%), and independently reconfirmed in CARE's 19 June 2025 press release on the same entity (https://www.careratings.com/upload/CompanyFiles/PR/202506130628_GSPL_India_Gasnet_Limited.pdf, same false-negative pattern, confirmed manually), which repeats the identical 52/26/11/11 split. Two independent CARE Ratings vintages plus the wiki-cited annual report all agree -- tier high. Flagging as an aside (not used, not cited): a low-quality secondary aggregator, offshore-technology.com's marketdata page for this pipeline, incorrectly lists 'Oil and Natural Gas' (ONGC) among the owners -- this is not supported by either PNGRB's register, CARE Ratings, or the GSPL annual report, and is disregarded as that source's own error. DUPLICATE check against the 35-row India roster: P5533 (Bhatinda-Gurdaspur) picks up immediately where this pipeline ends at Bhatinda and is a SEPARATE PNGRB-authorised asset (register item 2, its own distinct authorisation date/length/capacity) operated by the same entity (GIGL) -- not the same physical pipe as P0941, correctly two rows. P5411 ('Phase II', construction status, 763 km, same PipelineName/Capacity/Owner) is the documented partially-commissioned pairing this sweep's scope guidance anticipated (GEM's operating-length/under-construction-length split of one PNGRB-authorised asset into two rows); P0941 (1,177 km) + P5411 (763 km) = 1,940 km, matching PNGRB's authorised length for this asset almost exactly (1,940-1,943 km across editions) -- confirms the split is a granularity choice, not a duplicate or double-count.

validity.recommendation: Route to Update for a joint P0941/P5411 review, not a mechanical refresh: (1) LengthKnown=1,177 km and Capacity=80.11 MMSCMD were accurate for GEM's July-2023 vintage but are now stale -- PNGRB's current (31 May 2026) edition shows operating length 1,339 km and authorised/design capacity 83.1 MMSCMD for this asset; (2) before applying that refresh, reconcile it against CARE Ratings' August-2024 COD declaration (1,417.80 km completed, 276.2 km permanently de-scoped from the financed project) and the June-2025 update (three spur lines still under active construction, one 130 km Bhatinda-Jalandhar trunk stalled on RoW) -- PNGRB's 'under construction' 604 km bucket and CARE's 'de-scoped' framing describe overlapping but not identical things and need a human read before either P0941's operating length or P5411's construction length/status is edited; (3) verify StartYear1=2022 -- CARE's own filings put Phase-I-in-GIGL's-own-numbering (442 km) as operational since November 2018, four years earlier, and GEM's 'Phase I' (1,177 km) does not map 1:1 onto GIGL's company phase-I/II/III scheme, so 2022 may reflect a later commissioning milestone rather than first gas; confirm which milestone GEM intends before changing it.
validity.researcher_notes: LENGTH/CAPACITY: cross-checked GEM's LengthKnown=1177.00/Capacity=80.11 MMSCMD against a sequence of PNGRB's own monthly/periodic NGPL registers, fetched independently via Wayback Machine archives of pngrb.gov.in's own PDFs (none GEM- or wiki-authored): 31.03.2022 edition (op. length 1,030 km / UC 910 km / capacity 80.11 MMSCMD -- https://web.archive.org/web/20231225124427/https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/NGPL-23052022.pdf), a Dec-2022 edition (op. 1,153 km / UC 787 km / capacity 80.11 -- https://web.archive.org/web/20240628103021/https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/NGPL-02122022.pdf), and a 21.02.2024 edition (op. 1,200 km / UC 740 km / capacity 80.11 -- https://web.archive.org/web/20241121235526/https://www.pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/NGPL-21022024.pdf). GEM's recorded value of 1,177 km sits exactly between the Dec-2022 (1,153) and Feb-2024 (1,200) readings, and the LastUpdated date (2023-07-20) matches the wiki's own citation retrieval date for PNGRB (cite_note-:3-4, 'Retrieved 2023-07-20') -- so the sheet value was correct for its vintage, corroborated by two independent regulator snapshots bracketing it in time, not a research error. However it is now materially stale: the CURRENT PNGRB edition (31 May 2026, cited above) shows operating length 1,339 km (+162 km / +13.8% vs GEM) and authorised+design capacity 83.1 MMSCMD (+2.99 / +3.6% vs GEM) -- this remains an actively-commissioning 'partially commissioned' asset (target completion date in the current PNGRB edition has slipped to Jun-2026). STATUS COMPLEXITY (why this is not a simple refresh): CARE Ratings' 30-Aug-2024 press release (cited above) states the ENTIRE financed project achieved commercial operations date (COD) on 22 August 2024 for 1,417.80 km, with the remaining 276.2 km of originally-scoped construction 'de-scoped' (removed from the debt-financed project and its associated debt surrendered, ₹5,076cr sanctioned reduced to ₹4,289cr). The June-2025 update (cited above) clarifies this did NOT mean abandonment: GIGL is still actively building three spur lines (NFL Bhatinda, HPCL Mittal Energy, Jodhpur connectivity -- expected complete FY26/FY27, funded separately outside the original project debt) while a 130 km Bhatinda-Jalandhar trunk section has 'no movement... due to RoW issues.' This means PNGRB's current 604 km 'under construction' figure and CARE's 276.2 km 'de-scoped' figure describe an overlapping but not identical picture (differently-funded, differently-timed pieces of the same residual scope), and it is not safe for me to mechanically translate either into a length/status edit on P0941 or its paired construction row P5411 -- that judgment call belongs to Update. STARTYEAR: GEM records StartYear1=2022 for this 'Phase I' (1,177 km) row. CARE Ratings (both vintages, independently) states 'phase-I, including 442 kms of natural gas pipeline, achieved commercial operations date (COD) in November 2018' -- but GIGL's own phase-I/II/III numbering (442 / ~944 / ~308 km per CARE) does not correspond to GEM's two-row operating/under-construction split (1,177 / 763 km), so I cannot conclude GEM's 'Phase I' StartYear should simply become 2018; it may legitimately represent a later cumulative-commissioning milestone. Flagging as an open question rather than asserting a replacement value. Other total-length figures encountered in the course of this research (offshore-technology.com's 'upcoming... 1,834km', DMS Projects' 'approximate 1625km... Completed', CARE's own 'total project of 1,693.50 kms') all disagree with each other and with PNGRB/GEM's ~1,940-1,943 km authorised total -- illustrating that 'total length' for this pipeline varies by scope definition (original vs. revised vs. de-scoped authorisation) and reinforcing that PNGRB's authorised-length register, which GEM's split already tracks, is the most defensible anchor; not proposing any of those competing totals as a replacement.
